name: Tab
description: Represents the tab of a chart or a worksheet.
remarks: Use the Tab property of the Chart object or Worksheet object to return a Tab object. After a Tab object is returned, you can use the ColorIndex property to determine the settings of a tab for a chart or worksheet.
example:
Sub CheckTab()

 ' Determine if color index of 1st tab is set to none.
 If Worksheets(1).Tab.ColorIndex = xlColorIndexNone Then
 MsgBox "The color index is set to none for the first " & _
 "worksheet tab."
 Else
 MsgBox "The color index for the tab of the first worksheet " & _
 "is not set none."
 End If

End Sub

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Color
properties.description: Returns or sets the primary color of the object, as shown in the table in the remarks section. Use the RGB function to create a color value. Read/write Variant.

properties.name: ColorIndex
properties.description: Returns or sets a Variant value that represents the color of the specified worksheet tab or chart tab.

properties.name: ThemeColor
properties.description: Returns or sets the theme color in the applied color scheme that is associated with the specified object. Read/write XlThemeColor.

properties.name: TintAndShade
properties.description: Returns or sets a Single that lightens or darkens a color.
